We use cookies to enhance your browsing experience, serve personalized ads or content, and analyze our traffic. By clicking "Accept All", you consent to our use of cookies.

We use cookies to help you navigate efficiently and perform certain functions. You will find detailed information about all cookies under each consent category below.

The cookies that are categorized as "Necessary" are stored on your browser as they are essential for enabling the basic functionalities of the site. ...Show more

Necessary cookies are required to enable the basic features of this site, such as providing secure log-in or adjusting your consent preferences. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable data.

Functional cookies help perform certain functionalities like sharing the content of the website on social media platforms, collecting feedback, and other third-party features.

Advertisement cookies are used to provide visitors with customized advertisements based on the pages you visited previously and to analyze the effectiveness of the ad campaigns.

_**Benefit Street Partners (BSP), Franklin Templeton’s alternative credit manager, has added a 14-person investment team from Encina Lender Finance through a transaction that expands its private asset-backed finance platform, according to a statement from the firms.**_

The team will continue to manage and originate investments under the strategy. Alongside the move, a new fund backed by Franklin Templeton and BSP-affiliated funds acquired a seed portfolio comprising approximately $480m of commitments originated by Encina.

The incoming team provides senior secured, unitranche and first-out financing to consumer and commercial asset originators across the US and Canada. Investments are backed by pools of assets including consumer loans, credit card receivables and small business loans.

The transaction broadens BSP’s middle-market financing capabilities, with its asset-backed finance platform now covering corporate asset-backed lending, equipment leasing, aircraft leasing, consumer finance and lender finance.

Following the transaction, the combined platform has access to approximately 100 investment professionals and a track record dating back to 2013. It has completed more than $10bn of investments since inception, and BSP estimates it can originate more than $3bn annually.

BSP chief executive David Manlowe said the addition would expand the firm’s origination capabilities and range of financing solutions as institutional investor demand for asset-backed finance grows.

Franklin Templeton chief executive Jenny Johnson said the group was selectively deploying its balance sheet to support the expansion of its private markets business.

Franklin Templeton managed $1.8tn in assets as at 30 September 2026, including more than $300bn in alternatives. BSP managed approximately $97bn.
